title: Failover dashboard mock + metric/alert notes (draft)
body:
Context
- This is the working doc for the “Regional failover automation upgrade” dashboards + alert candidates.
- Target audience: on-call SRE + Platform/Routing (Smart Routing) + Infra (capacity/network).
- This doc is intentionally scrappy; final spec lives in Confluence once we stop changing names weekly.

Goals for dashboards
1) Fast answer to “is a region unhealthy?” (w/ enough signal to decide failover vs degrade)
2) Fast answer to “what is the system doing right now?” (state machine + automation actions)
3) Fast answer to “who is impacted and how bad?” (customer tier, model, route)
4) Reduce alert noise vs last incidents; move paging to burn-rate + state transition events

Non-goals
- Not building a generic ‘all infra’ dashboard. This is failover-focused.
- Not adding per-host deep dives (link out to existing infra dashboards).

Dashboards: proposed layout (Console + Grafana)

A) Region Health Overview (single pane)
- Top row: Region status pills (per region): HEALTHY / DEGRADED / FAILOVERING / FAILED_OVER / HOLD_DOWN
- Each pill shows: last transition time + “primary signal that caused status”
- Panels:
  1. Request success rate (2xx/3xx) by region
  2. 5xx rate by region (stacked: upstream, routing, inference)
  3. Latency heatmap by region (p50/p95/p99) for “core routes”
  4. Saturation: queue depth + GPU headroom by region
  5. Network path health summary (synthetic probes)

B) Failover State Machine + Audit Trail
- Timeline panel: state transitions with annotations
  - “trigger_evaluated”, “safe_to_failover_failed: capacity”, “progressive_failover_started”, “rollback”, “hold_down_start/end”
- Table: last 50 actions
  - columns: timestamp, from_state, to_state, reason_code, evaluator_version, actor (automation / manual override), runbook_link
- Panel: current routing policy deltas (what changed)
  - traffic split by region for scoped routes / tiers

C) Customer Impact (by tier/model/route)
- Panels:
  1. Error rate by tier (free/pro/enterprise) within affected region
  2. Impacted tokens/sec and requests/sec moved cross-region (before vs after)
  3. “Fallback events” rate: model_variant fallback, degraded mode (load shed / timeout tighten)
  4. Streaming disconnect rate by region (important: this was the customer-visible symptom during packet loss incident)

D) Safety Checks (Safe-to-failover)
- Panels:
  1. Target region capacity readiness: GPU headroom %, queue depth, scheduler saturation
  2. Dependency health for target region: KV cache store, auth, policy store, edge/DNS controller
  3. Cross-region link health (where relevant)
- Callouts: “Failover blocked because …”

E) Deep Links section
- Links to:
  - runbook: Automated region failover
  - region health signal contract
  - incident bot commands
  - infra DNS/edge routing plan

Metric naming proposal

Principles
- We need:
  - stable metric names (avoid churn)
  - consistent label schema so we can group/aggregate
  - reason codes on decisions (so we can build explainability + reduce pager spam)
- Avoid: one metric per route/model (explodes cardinality). Prefer labels but keep bounded.

Namespace
Option 1 (preferred): redwood.failover.*
Option 2: redwood.routing.failover.*

Core dimensions/labels (try to keep consistent across all failover metrics)
- env: staging|prod
- source_region: us-east|us-west|eu-central|… (the region being evaluated / degraded)
- target_region: (for actions)
- scope: global|tier:enterprise|route:chat.completions|model:llama3-70b|customer:<id> (NOTE: keep scope values bounded; see below)
- customer_tier: free|pro|enterprise
- route_group: chat|embeddings|rerank|admin (bounded)
- reason_code: enum (see below)
- action: evaluate|degrade|failover_start|failover_step|rollback|hold_down

IMPORTANT: scope label
- Do NOT put raw customer_id in metrics by default.
- Proposal: only include customer_id in audit log events (and in a dedicated low-volume metric behind a gate), not in standard dashboards.

Reason codes (draft enum)
- high_5xx
- high_tail_latency
- upstream_dependency_unhealthy
- capacity_saturation
- network_path_loss
- synthetic_probe_fail
- manual_override
- safe_to_failover_capacity_block
- safe_to_failover_dependency_block
- config_error

Metrics (draft list)

1) Health signal aggregation output
- redwood.failover.region_health_score (gauge 0..100)
  - labels: env, source_region
  - note: optional; score is nice for UI but risky as a pager input
- redwood.failover.signal.status (gauge 0/1)
  - labels: env, source_region, signal_name (bounded: error_rate, tail_latency, probe, dep_health, saturation)
- redwood.failover.signal.value (gauge)
  - labels: env, source_region, signal_name
  - NOTE: only for a small set of signals; keep bounded

2) Trigger engine
- redwood.failover.trigger.evaluate_total (counter)
  - labels: env, source_region, trigger_name, result (true|false)
- redwood.failover.trigger.current_state (gauge enum)
  - labels: env, source_region
  - states: 0 healthy, 1 degraded, 2 failovering, 3 failed_over, 4 hold_down
- redwood.failover.trigger.reason (gauge 0/1)
  - labels: env, source_region, reason_code
  - note: set to 1 for the active dominant reason(s)

3) Orchestrator actions
- redwood.failover.action_total (counter)
  - labels: env, source_region, target_region, action, scope, result (success|fail)
- redwood.failover.action_duration_seconds (histogram)
  - labels: env, action

4) Progressive failover
- redwood.failover.traffic_split (gauge 0..1)
  - labels: env, source_region, target_region, scope
  - value = fraction of scoped traffic routed to target_region

5) Safety checks
- redwood.failover.safe_to_failover.status (gauge 0/1)
  - labels: env, source_region, target_region, check_name (capacity|dependency|policy_sanity)
- redwood.failover.safe_to_failover.block_total (counter)
  - labels: env, source_region, target_region, check_name, reason_code

6) Customer impact/supporting SLO views (likely exist already; just ensuring labels)
- redwood.inference.requests_total / redwood.inference.errors_total
  - ensure: region, customer_tier, route_group, error_type
- redwood.inference.latency_seconds (histogram)
  - ensure: region, customer_tier, route_group
- redwood.inference.streaming.disconnect_total
  - ensure: region, customer_tier, route_group

Alert candidates (draft)

Pager philosophy (aligned w/ Aisha’s SLO guidance)
- Page when:
  (a) error budget burn indicates sustained customer impact AND
  (b) automation is in a state requiring human oversight (failovering, repeated rollbacks, hold-down loops)
- Ticket/Slack-only when: single-signal noisy events, transient probe loss, brief spikes.

1) Multi-window burn-rate alerts (primary)
- Availability burn (example thresholds; final comes from SLO doc)
  - Page: 14x for 5m AND 2x for 1h (per region, per route_group)
  - Warn: 6x for 5m AND 1x for 6h
- Latency burn (p99)
  - Page: 14x for 5m AND 2x for 1h (if we have latency SLO per route_group)

2) Failover automation state alerts (secondary)
- “Failover stuck”
  - Condition: trigger_current_state = failovering for > 10m
  - Include: source_region, current scope, last action, last error
- “Flap detected”
  - Condition: > 3 state transitions between degraded/healthy within 30m
  - Action: page SRE (this is exactly what we want to prevent; indicates threshold/hysteresis mismatch)
- “Safe-to-failover blocked during active incident”
  - Condition: error budget burn paging active AND safe_to_failover.status=0 for capacity/dependency
  - This is a high-signal heads-up: we’re burning but can’t fail over automatically.

3) Synthetic probe alerts (do NOT page by default)
- Slack-only: probe loss > X% for > 5m, only if corroborated by real traffic errors/latency.

Noise notes from prior incidents (what we should NOT repeat)

From Slack incident threads (1709664012, 1709669820) + general on-call feedback:
- Probe-only paging was noisy:
  - False positives when a single probe POP had issues or when a path was temporarily rate-limited.
  - Action: probes should be a contributing signal, not sole pager trigger.
- Per-host latency paging caused a “p99 of one box” rabbit hole:
  - It did not correlate to customer impact.
  - Action: aggregate to region + route_group + tier; link to host drilldown for debugging.
- Single-window alerts flapped:
  - A 2–3 minute spike paged, then immediately recovered.
  - Action: multi-window/multi-burn + minimum duration.
- Too many “symptom” alerts, not enough “system doing something” context:
  - We got paged for 5xx, then had to manually check if routing changes were happening.
  - Action: annotate action timeline + post transitions in #incidents.

Dashboard mock (ASCII)

[Region Health Overview]
- Region: us-east (pill: DEGRADED)  last_transition: 12:41:10Z  reason: network_path_loss

Panels (left to right)
1) Availability (success rate)
2) 5xx rate (stacked by error_type)
3) Latency p50/p95/p99
4) Queue depth + GPU headroom
5) Probe loss % + dependency health summary

[Failover State]
- Current state: DEGRADED
- Automation mode: monitor-only / active (flag)
- Progressive failover: 10% (scope: tier:free + route_group:chat)

Action timeline (last 60m)
- 12:41 degrade_start reason=network_path_loss
- 12:44 safe_to_failover check=capacity result=pass
- 12:45 progressive_failover_started 5%
- 12:47 progressive_failover_step 10%

Open questions / TODO
- Metric naming final decision (Allison): redwood.failover.* vs redwood.routing.failover.*
- What is the authoritative region list + naming scheme (Infra): us-east vs use1 vs iad?
- Label normalization:
  - route_group mapping (Platform): need a stable mapping table in code so dashboards don’t drift
  - error_type taxonomy (SRE): upstream vs platform vs customer-cancel vs timeout
- Where do we store “audit log events”? (Felix + Ethan)
  - We need durable events for postmortems; metrics are not enough.
- Cardinality risks:
  - scope label must stay bounded; propose only {global, tier:<tier>, route_group:<group>, model_class:<class>}
- Alert ownership:
  - Who gets paged for “safe-to-failover blocked” (SRE primary, Infra secondary?)

Notes from recent review (2025-04-16)
- Aisha: page should be driven by error budget burn; state machine alerts are supplements.
- Miles: add explicit visualization of hold-down timer remaining (so on-call doesn’t guess when automation will re-attempt).
- Mina: needs “what traffic moved?” panel that’s easy to screenshot for incident comms.

Next steps
- Sergio: implement v0 dashboard panels + annotations in observability-pack PR (in progress)
- Allison: confirm metric name + label set by end of week (so routing team stops renaming)
- Felix: wire audit event feed to dashboard table (can be placeholder until storage finalized)
- Logan: verify ingestion pipeline can handle added histograms (action duration) without dropping samples
